name: West Bank (Bus Station Side)
tagline: Arrival gateway and everyday village life
description: The west side of the Nam Ou holds the bus and minivan station, small shops, local eateries, and the boat landing for trips upriver. It is the practical, workaday half of Nong Khiaw where most transport connections begin and everyday village life carries on around the market and roadside stalls.
vibe: Practical, local, and a little more workaday than the far bank
bestFor: Easy transport access, cheaper local food, and short stays
pros: Right by the bus, minivan, and boat departure points
Local shops and cheap Lao eateries close at hand
Handy base if you are moving on quickly
cons: Fewer river-view bungalows than the east bank
More traffic and transport noise near the station

name: East Bank (Guesthouse and Viewpoint Side)
tagline: Riverside bungalows and the traveller heart of the village
description: Across the bridge, the east bank is where most travellers stay. Riverside bungalows, hammock-strung guesthouses, laid-back cafes, and trek and boat operators line the road, and the trailheads for the famous viewpoints start nearby. It is the relaxed, scenic core of Nong Khiaw's small traveller scene.
vibe: Mellow, scenic, and social in an easygoing backpacker way
bestFor: Slow travellers wanting river views and viewpoint access
pros: Best riverside bungalows and karst-mountain views
Closest to the Phadeng and Sleeping Woman trailheads
Cafes, restaurants, and tour operators all within a short walk
cons: Wifi and power are especially variable in the bungalows
Can feel quiet and sleepy outside the dry season

name: Phadeng Viewpoint and Sleeping Woman Trailhead Area
tagline: Where the steep climbs to the mist-filled views begin
description: Just off the east bank sit the trailheads for the Phadeng (Pha Daeng) viewpoint and the Sleeping Woman viewpoint. These are not places to sleep but the reason many people come: steep, sweaty climbs reward you with panoramas of karst peaks rising above the Nam Ou and its famous morning mist.
vibe: Adventurous, sweaty, and utterly rewarding at sunrise
bestFor: Hikers and sunrise chasers wanting the iconic views
pros: Home to Nong Khiaw's most iconic viewpoints
Unforgettable sunrise panoramas over a sea of mist
Trailheads are within walking distance of east-bank lodging
cons: Steep, strenuous climbs that can be slippery when wet
Small entrance fees and no accommodation at the top

name: Muang Ngoi (Upriver Village)
tagline: The roadless riverside hideaway further up the Nam Ou
description: An hour or so upriver by longtail boat, Muang Ngoi is an even more remote and roadless village hemmed in by karst cliffs. With no through road, no nightlife, and only patchy electricity, it is Nong Khiaw dialled further toward stillness, favoured by travellers wanting to disconnect completely among caves and rice paddies.
vibe: Even quieter, remoter, and more off-grid than Nong Khiaw
bestFor: Deep unplugging, hammock days, and river-and-cave wandering
pros: Stunning karst scenery and nearby caves and villages
Even cheaper and slower than Nong Khiaw
cons: Reachable only by boat, with very basic infrastructure
Electricity and connectivity are minimal or absent
